Published online:
    September 1, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (Japan, US, Australia, Europe, Germany)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    A synchronized global bond selloff is accelerating, with Japan's 10-year JGB yield breaching 3% for the first time since 1996. The rout is driven by oil-fueled inflation fears, aggressive sovereign and corporate issuance (AI-driven hyperscaler funding + $40T US debt load), and a hawkish pivot from both the Fed (under Chair Kevin Warsh post-Jackson Hole) and the BoJ. Markets are repricing rate hike expectations globally, with Germany's 10-year at a 14-year high. The JGB crossing 3% is described as a regime change — unwinding Japan's role as global fixed income anchor and threatening carry trade dynamics.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — US 10-year Treasuries hit 4.786% (highest since early last year), Fed Chair Warsh explicitly struck a hawkish tone at Jackson Hole, and US fiscal concerns ($40T debt) are cited as a core driver of the selloff.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly YES)
Probability of increase: 80%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (effectively NO)
Probability of holding: 10%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO)
Probability of decrease: 10%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (Decisively more hawkish than before — Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole posture, Treasury Secretary Bessent pressuring BoJ to tighten, markets concerned central banks are already behind the curve, and US 10-year yields surging to multi-year highs all point to a strongly hawkish near-term trajectory)
